KMI-style Shariah screening on PSX

KMI and similar screens publish methodologies and stock lists so investors can see which companies currently meet a defined Shariah framework. Think of them as rulebooks with updates — not permanent halal stamps.

Indexes vs personal rulings

An index methodology is one structured approach. Your advisor may add stricter filters or different interpretations.

Always know which list you are following and when it was last reviewed.

What typically gets examined

Public methodologies usually discuss business segments and selected financial ratios. The official documentation is the source of truth for definitions and thresholds.

Third-party apps and posts can lag behind reconstitutions — verify against the publisher when stakes are high.

Using a compliant universe in practice

Many investors build watchlists from a current universe, then apply normal fundamental analysis: profitability, debt, valuation and governance.

Screening answers “eligible under this method?” — not “will this make money?”

Portfolio hygiene still applies

If you invest in screened names, track lots, dividends and sells like any other portfolio. Faith-conscious investing does not remove the need for records or risk management.
